corrected_draft.description_long: The White House fact sheet said OPM estimated that 50,000 positions, about 2 percent of the federal workforce, could ultimately be moved into Schedule Policy/Career. The category was described as career positions filled through existing merit-based hiring, with employees expected to implement the law and administration policies. This was an OPM proposal and estimate, not evidence that 50,000 employees had already been reclassified or that an actual list of “disloyal” workers had been created. corrected_draft.title: Bondi creates working group to review Trump investigations
corrected_draft.description_short: Attorney General Pam Bondi created a Justice Department working group to review Trump-related investigations, including state investigations in New York.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On February 5, 2025, Attorney General Pam Bondi announced a Justice Department Weaponization Working Group to examine investigations she described as politicized. corrected_draft.description_long: On February 5, 2025, Attorney General Pam Bondi created a Justice Department “Weaponization Working Group” to review what she described as politicized justice. The Washington Post reported that the group would begin with federal criminal cases brought against Donald Trump by special counsel Jack Smith. Bondi also ordered an examination of alleged federal cooperation in Trump’s New York criminal and civil investigations, which were conducted by state authorities, including Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg. The report separately describes acting Deputy Attorney General Emil Bove’s personnel actions and review of roughly 5,000 FBI agents who had worked on January 6 cases. Those were separate directives and should not be folded into a claim that DOJ opened a criminal investigation of Bragg. The article documents a review directive, not a criminal probe into the Manhattan DA, and does not establish that the federal review produced charges or findings against him.

remaining_gap: Bondi’s Feb. 5 Weaponization Working Group review directive is supported. It is not evidence DOJ opened a criminal investigation of Manhattan DA Bragg.
